docs.title: maoorf — Machine-Actionable OECD Omics Reporting Framework
docs.text:
A modular LinkML data model for the OECD Omics Reporting Framework (OORF), designed to make regulatory toxicology omics metadata machine-actionable, extensible, and FAIR.

Work in Progress & Community Initiative

  • Community-Driven Effort: This machine-actionable schema is not officially endorsed by the OECD. It is an independent formalization effort initiated by the toxicology community within PARC (Partnership for the Assessment of Risks from Chemicals) based on the published OECD Omics Reporting Framework (2023).
  • Work in Progress: This repository is under active development. The current schema provides a 1:1 structural translation of the official OORF Excel reporting templates (with exact element mappings to oecd_oorf_2023) as the foundation for upcoming ontology alignment and FAIRification.
  • AI-Assisted Development: The initial translation of the OECD OORF Excel template and guidance document into modular LinkML was assisted by generative AI (Google Gemini / Antigravity) under human direction and is actively undergoing domain-expert review and curation.

docs.title: Module Entry Points
docs.text:
Each OORF submission (OORF) is composed of the following modular building blocks:

OORF Section Entry Point Class Purpose Root Submission OORF Top-level container combining one SSRM, one TERM, one or more DAPRMs, one or more DARMs, and a FileManifestEntry list Module 1: Study Summary SSRM High-level study overview, identifiers, and executive summary of the experiment, assays, and analyses Module 2: Toxicology Experiment TERM Study rationale, test/control chemical items, in vivo / in vitro test system characteristics, study design, treatment conditions, and sample collection Module 3: Data Acquisition & Processing (DAPRM) DAPRM (Abstract) Base class for omics assay acquisition and pre-processing modules:
  • 3.1 Microarray: MicroarrayDAPRM
  • 3.2 RNA-Seq & Targeted RNA-Seq: RNASeqDAPRM
  • 3.3 qRT-PCR Array: QRTPCRDAPRM
  • 3.4 Mass Spectrometry (LC-MS / GC-MS): MassSpectrometryDAPRM
  • 3.5 NMR Metabolomics: NMRDAPRM
Module 4: Data Analysis (DARM) DARM (Abstract) Base class for statistical and bioinformatics analysis modules (inherits common inputs and outputs slots):
  • 4.1 Differentially Abundant Molecules: DAMDARM
  • 4.2 Multivariate Statistical Analysis: MVADARM
  • 4.3 Benchmark Dose (BMD) Modeling: BMDDARM
  • 8. Enriched Biological Pathways (Draft): EBPDARM
File Manifest & Shared Entities FileManifestEntry Tracks all machine-readable data objects, metadata tables, scripts, and MD5 checksums. Shared structures also include SoftwareDocumentation and AssayExperimentalDesign

docs.title: About maoorf
docs.text:
maoorf is a machine-actionable formalization of the OECD Omics Reporting Framework (OORF) built with LinkML (Linked Data Modeling Language).

Disclaimer & Project Status

  1. Not Yet Endorsed by the OECD: This schema is an independent community effort started by the toxicology community in PARC (Partnership for the Assessment of Risks from Chemicals). It has not yet been formally reviewed or endorsed by the OECD.
  2. Work in Progress: The model is under active development. In its current stage, it closely mirrors the structure of the 2023 OECD OORF Excel reporting templates so that existing filled-in templates can be validated and converted into JSON/YAML while preserving exact 1:1 mappings (oecd_oorf_2023) for SSSOM generation. Subsequent iterations will link slots to domain ontologies and controlled vocabularies to further FAIRify regulatory omics reporting.
  3. AI-Assisted Development: The initial translation of the OECD OORF Excel template and guidance document into modular LinkML was assisted by generative AI (Google Gemini / Antigravity) under human direction and is actively undergoing domain-expert review and curation.

docs.title: Upstream OECD Specification
docs.text:
This schema derives from the published OECD guidance document and reporting templates:

OECD (2023), OECD Omics Reporting Framework (OORF): Guidance on reporting elements for the regulatory use of omics data from laboratory-based toxicology studies, OECD Series on Testing and Assessment, No. 390, OECD Publishing, Paris, https://doi.org/10.1787/6bb2e6ce-en.

docs.title: Extensible Modular Design
docs.text:
Because omics technologies and data analysis methods continuously evolve, the OORF is designed as a modular framework. maoorf reflects this modularity in LinkML:

  • OORF: The root container representing a complete study report.
  • SSRM & TERM: Study summary and toxicology experiment modules.
  • DAPRM: Abstract base class for platform-specific Data Acquisition and Processing Reporting Modules (MicroarrayDAPRM, RNASeqDAPRM, QRTPCRDAPRM, MassSpectrometryDAPRM, NMRDAPRM).
  • DARM: Abstract base class for Data Analysis Reporting Modules (DAMDARM, MVADARM, BMDDARM, EBPDARM).

External researchers and tool developers can define their own custom DAPRM or DARM modules by subclassing DAPRM or DARM in a standalone YAML file. See the schema directory README for a step-by-step guide.

docs.title: AI-Assisted Development Disclosure
docs.text: The modular LinkML architecture, extraction of reporting elements, descriptions, and provider notes from the official OECD OORF (2023) Excel template and Guidance PDF, and the conversion of example datasets were developed with the assistance of generative AI (Google Gemini via Antigravity). All architectural decisions, modeling constraints, and validation workflows are directed and reviewed by the project maintainers, who take full responsibility for the curated specification.

docs.title: Class: AssayExperimentalDesign
docs.text:
Assay Experimental Design

__

In order to ensure that the omics data were analysed properly, the end-user must have a clear description of which samples were used in the analysis, how many samples there are per experimental group, and how they may be assayed together/measured simultaneously or not. In addition, the end-user can use this information to perform post hoc power analyses, as well as estimates for Type M (magnitude) and Type S (sign) error, which are equally, if not more, informative in assessing data quality and the likelihood of drawing erroneous conclusions.

      or factor at a minimum. Should include the sample IDs that can be used to match
      across the report.'

      group or factor. Should include the sample IDs that be used to match across
      the report. Information may be provided in a data object. If such information
      is included in a data object with this submission, please list the file name
      here.
    from_schema: https://w3id.org/eu-parc/maoorf

    owner: AssayExperimentalDesign

    recommended: true
  covariance:

      Identification of which samples may exhibit covariance (examples include: assayed
      on the same day, assayed in parallel, assayed on the same physical platform
      (eg chip/glass slide, cartridge, etc for transcriptomics; LC-MS analytical batch,
      etc for metabolomics), processed using the same wash solutions or reagents,
      processed using the same master mixes (transcriptomics only), littermates in
      the exposure study, animals which are housed together, etc). Provide an explicit
      statement if there is no reason to believe covariance exists between samples,
      and a justification to support this assertion.'
    comments:
    - Identify which samples may exhibit covariance. This information may be provided
      as a data object. If such information is included in a data object with this
      submission, please list the file name here. If there is no reason to believe
      covaraince exists between samples, please provide a justification of this assertion
      in this reporting field.

docs.title: Class: BMDBenchmarkDoseModeling
docs.text:
Benchmark Dose Modeling

__

Parameters and model selection criteria for Benchmark Dose (BMD) modelling.

docs.title: Induced
docs.text:
name: BMDBenchmarkDoseModeling
description: 'Benchmark Dose Modeling


  Parameters and model selection criteria for Benchmark Dose (BMD) modelling.'
from_schema: https://w3id.org/eu-parc/maoorf
exact_mappings:
- oecd_oorf_2023:4.3.5
attributes:
  bmd_modeling_approach:
    name: bmd_modeling_approach
    description: 'BMD Modeling Approach


      As noted above there are different approaches (e.g. parametric and non-parametric
      approaches) to dose response modelling. The specific method used should be specified.'
    from_schema: https://w3id.org/eu-parc/maoorf/modules/darm/bmd
    exact_mappings:
    - oecd_oorf_2023:4.3.5.1
    rank: 1000
    owner: BMDBenchmarkDoseModeling
    domain_of:
    - BMDBenchmarkDoseModeling
    range: string
    recommended: true
  method_for_final_estimation_of_msd_bmd:
    name: method_for_final_estimation_of_msd_bmd
    description: 'Method for Final Estimation of MSD BMD


      There are two general approaches for identifying a final potency estimate for
      a given feature - best model selection and model averaging. With the best model
      approach a single best model is used to derive the BMD; whereas, model averaging
      uses a weighted average to derive a final BMD estimate. In the case of non-parametric
      modelling, typically only a single model fitting process is performed, hence
      there isn''t a best model or models to average. In this case the method for
      final estimation of BMD is simply the modelling approach.'
    from_schema: https://w3id.org/eu-parc/maoorf/modules/darm/bmd
    exact_mappings:
    - oecd_oorf_2023:4.3.5.2
    rank: 1000
    owner: BMDBenchmarkDoseModeling
    domain_of:
    - BMDBenchmarkDoseModeling
    range: string
    recommended: true
  list_of_models_fit_to_data:
    name: list_of_models_fit_to_data
    description: 'List of Models Fit to the Data


      In the case of parametric modelling (with or without model averaging) a set
      of models that represent different dose-response shapes are used to model the
      data. Report all models fit to the data in the modelling process.'
    from_schema: https://w3id.org/eu-parc/maoorf/modules/darm/bmd
    exact_mappings:
    - oecd_oorf_2023:4.3.5.3
    rank: 1000
    owner: BMDBenchmarkDoseModeling
    domain_of:
    - BMDBenchmarkDoseModeling
    range: string
    recommended: true
  model_averaging_approach:
    name: model_averaging_approach
    description: 'Model Averaging Approach


      When performing model averaging, a variety of mathematical approaches can be
      used that can impact the eventual BMD estimate of an MSD. Record what method
      was employed and any other associated critical parameters associated with the
      averaging process. If model averaging is not employed, indicate NA (not applicable)
      in this section.'
    comments:
    - If model averaging was not used in the analysis, report "NA".
    from_schema: https://w3id.org/eu-parc/maoorf/modules/darm/bmd
    exact_mappings:
    - oecd_oorf_2023:4.3.5.4
    rank: 1000
    owner: BMDBenchmarkDoseModeling
    domain_of:
    - BMDBenchmarkDoseModeling
    range: string
    recommended: true
  method_for_determining_bmr:
    name: method_for_determining_bmr
    description: 'Method for Determining Benchmark Response (BMR; aka BMR Type)


      There are a number of ways of determining a critical response threshold, i.e.
      a BMR. Two examples are the multiple of standard deviation from control or the
      relative deviation (percent change) from control. Report the method used to
      determine the BMR.'
    from_schema: https://w3id.org/eu-parc/maoorf/modules/darm/bmd
    exact_mappings:
    - oecd_oorf_2023:4.3.5.5
    rank: 1000
    owner: BMDBenchmarkDoseModeling
    domain_of:
    - BMDBenchmarkDoseModeling
    range: string
    recommended: true
  benchmark_response_bmr_factor:
    name: benchmark_response_bmr_factor
    description: 'Benchmark Response (BMR, aka BMR Factor)


      The BMR is the degree of change relative to control that is deemed to either
      be statistically or toxicologically relevant for the study. The threshold that
      was applied in the modelling process should be recorded.'
    from_schema: https://w3id.org/eu-parc/maoorf/modules/darm/bmd
    exact_mappings:
    - oecd_oorf_2023:4.3.5.6
    rank: 1000
    owner: BMDBenchmarkDoseModeling
    domain_of:
    - BMDBenchmarkDoseModeling
    range: string
    recommended: true
  number_of_fitting_iterations:
    name: number_of_fitting_iterations
    description: 'Number of Fitting Iterations


      In the case of individual parametric model fitting, a maximum number of iterations
      is typically allowed. This setting reflects the number of times a model is fit
      to an MSD to obtain a convergent estimate of the fit. If applicable, report
      the maximum number of iterations that were employed.'
    from_schema: https://w3id.org/eu-parc/maoorf/modules/darm/bmd
    exact_mappings:
    - oecd_oorf_2023:4.3.5.7
    rank: 1000
    owner: BMDBenchmarkDoseModeling
    domain_of:
    - BMDBenchmarkDoseModeling
    range: string
    recommended: true
  confidence_interval_of_bmd:
    name: confidence_interval_of_bmd
    description: 'Confidence Interval of the BMD (aka Confidence Level)


      This modelling parameter sets the confidence interval range that will be determined
      for the BMD values derived from each model fit to the data. Report how and what
      confidence intervals were derived.'
    from_schema: https://w3id.org/eu-parc/maoorf/modules/darm/bmd
    exact_mappings:
    - oecd_oorf_2023:4.3.5.8
    rank: 1000
    owner: BMDBenchmarkDoseModeling
    domain_of:
    - BMDBenchmarkDoseModeling
    range: string
    recommended: true
  power_parameter_restriction:
    name: power_parameter_restriction
    description: 'Power Parameter Restriction


      Often it is desirable to restrict the value of certain modelling parameters
      when performing parametric modelling. The most commonly restricted parameter
      is power and the restriction is most commonly applied when modelling the Hill
      and power models. Restricting the power parameter avoids biologically implausible
      fits to the data. Report if any of the model parameters were restricted in the
      modelling process and the specific restriction threshold.'
    comments:
    - If the power parameter used in any of the curve fits was restricted, report
      which model(s) and a value. Else, report "NA".
    from_schema: https://w3id.org/eu-parc/maoorf/modules/darm/bmd
    exact_mappings:
    - oecd_oorf_2023:4.3.5.9
    rank: 1000
    owner: BMDBenchmarkDoseModeling
    domain_of:
    - BMDBenchmarkDoseModeling
    range: string
    recommended: true
  variance_assumption:
    name: variance_assumption
    description: 'Variance Assumption


      Toxicology data are often heteroscedastic (i.e. the spread on the response distribution
      increases with dose). This is often referred to as non-constant variance. Different
      assumptions are made when data are assumed to be hetero vs homoscedastic, which
      can impact model fitting and BMD derivation. It is therefore necessary to document
      if constant or non-constant variance was assumed.'
    comments:
    - Report of constant or non-constant variance across doses was assumed for BMD
      modeling.
    from_schema: https://w3id.org/eu-parc/maoorf/modules/darm/bmd
    exact_mappings:
    - oecd_oorf_2023:4.3.5.10
    rank: 1000
    owner: BMDBenchmarkDoseModeling
    domain_of:
    - BMDBenchmarkDoseModeling
    range: string
    recommended: true
  model_selection:
    name: model_selection
    description: 'Model Selection


      In the case of the best model approach to parametric modelling, criteria for
      selection of the best model must be selected. There are several approaches that
      can be used to select the best model, all of which can impact eventual potency
      estimates for the MSDs. It is therefore necessary to document the method used
      to select the best model. If a best model approach is not applied (e.g. non-parametric
      modelling or model averaging, indicate NA (not applicable)).'
    comments:
    - State the rules used for best model selection.
    from_schema: https://w3id.org/eu-parc/maoorf/modules/darm/bmd
    exact_mappings:
    - oecd_oorf_2023:4.3.5.11
    owner: BMDBenchmarkDoseModeling
    domain_of:
    - TERMStudyRationale
    - BMDBenchmarkDoseModeling
    range: string
    recommended: true
  criteria_to_identify_extrapolated_models:
    name: criteria_to_identify_extrapolated_models
    description: 'Criteria to Identify Models that Extrapolate Outside the Dose Range


      When using the best model approach it is sometimes the case that due to dose
      selection the estimated BMD is well below the dose range. In this case the BMD
      can not be accurately estimated but it is desired to retain the MSD in the analysis.
      Document how flagged models were dealt with in the analysis.'
    comments:
    - Report any criteria that were used to identify results extrapolated outside
      of the dose range and how those instances were treated in the analysis.
    from_schema: https://w3id.org/eu-parc/maoorf/modules/darm/bmd
    exact_mappings:
    - oecd_oorf_2023:4.3.5.12
    rank: 1000
    owner: BMDBenchmarkDoseModeling
    domain_of:
    - BMDBenchmarkDoseModeling
    range: string
    recommended: true

docs.title: Class: BMDBiologicalSetLevelValues
docs.text:
Determination of Biological Entity or Biological Set Level BMD values

__

Biological entity or set annotations, acceptance criteria, active set criteria, and estimation method for set-level BMD values.

docs.title: Induced
docs.text:
name: BMDBiologicalSetLevelValues
description: 'Determination of Biological Entity or Biological Set Level BMD values


  Biological entity or set annotations, acceptance criteria, active set criteria,
  and estimation method for set-level BMD values.'
from_schema: https://w3id.org/eu-parc/maoorf
exact_mappings:
- oecd_oorf_2023:4.3.6
attributes:
  biological_entity_or_set_annotation_used:
    name: biological_entity_or_set_annotation_used
    description: 'Biological Entity or Biological Set Annotation Used for the Analysis


      In this section, document which biological entities (e.g. genes, metabolites)
      or biological sets (e.g. GO terms, KEGG pathways) were used in the analysis.
      The platform annotation (described above) should capture the versioning of the
      annotations used; however, if this is not the case (i.e. independent mappings
      of MSD to biological entities or sets were used) the source of these entities
      and any versioning should be documented'
    from_schema: https://w3id.org/eu-parc/maoorf/modules/darm/bmd
    exact_mappings:
    - oecd_oorf_2023:4.3.6.1
    owner: BMDBiologicalSetLevelValues
    domain_of:
    - BMDBiologicalSetLevelValues
    - EBPPathwayDatabase
    range: string
    recommended: true
  msd_acceptance_criteria:
    name: msd_acceptance_criteria
    description: 'MSD Acceptance Criteria for Use in Biological Entity of Set Analysis


      A number of criteria can be applied to the MSD models (e.g. the best fit model)
      to remove the fits where the quality is poor or the potency estimates are highly
      uncertain either due to noisy data or model extrapolation. Document all metrics
      and associated thresholds used in the analysis.'
    comments:
    - Document all metrics and thresholds used as acceptance criteria for MSD being
      input into Biological Entity or Set Analysis. If none, report "NA"
    from_schema: https://w3id.org/eu-parc/maoorf/modules/darm/bmd
    exact_mappings:
    - oecd_oorf_2023:4.3.6.2
    rank: 1000
    owner: BMDBiologicalSetLevelValues
    domain_of:
    - BMDBiologicalSetLevelValues
    range: string
    recommended: true
  criteria_for_identification_of_active_biological_sets:
    name: criteria_for_identification_of_active_biological_sets
    description: 'Criteria for Identification of "Active" Biological Sets


      In the case of parsing MSD into biological sets (e.g. pathways or gene ontologies),
      criteria must be set to identify the sets that are "active" (i.e. adequately
      populated by dose responsive MSD with acceptable model fits deemed to be responsive
      to treatment). Report the methods and thresholds set to define ''active'' biological
      sets.'
    from_schema: https://w3id.org/eu-parc/maoorf/modules/darm/bmd
    exact_mappings:
    - oecd_oorf_2023:4.3.6.3
    rank: 1000
    owner: BMDBiologicalSetLevelValues
    domain_of:
    - BMDBiologicalSetLevelValues
    range: string
    recommended: true
  method_of_estimating_set_bmd_bmdl_bmdu:
    name: method_of_estimating_set_bmd_bmdl_bmdu
    description: 'Method of Estimating the BMD, BMDL, and BMDU of the Individual Biological
      Entity or Biological Sets


      When MSD are sorted into sets this means a set contains several BMD values representative
      of each MSD in the set. When this happens, and the biological set is determined
      to be active (in the case of sets), a representative BMD, BMDL and BMDU value
      for the entire set can be determined. The choice of method will impact the estimate
      of potency for most biological entity sets so it is important that the method
      for deriving a representative BMD, BMDL and BMDU value be very clearly documented.'
    from_schema: https://w3id.org/eu-parc/maoorf/modules/darm/bmd
    exact_mappings:
    - oecd_oorf_2023:4.3.6.4
    rank: 1000
    owner: BMDBiologicalSetLevelValues
    domain_of:
    - BMDBiologicalSetLevelValues
    range: string
    recommended: true

docs.title: Class: BMDDARM
docs.text:
Data Analysis Reporting Module (DARM) for Benchmark Dose Analysis and Quantification of Biological Potency

__

This multi-omics compliant module specifies the information needed in order to assess benchmark dose (BMD) analysis of omics data and the subsequent derivation of an estimated BMD for a molecule (e.g. a transcript, protein or metabolite) or a set of molecules (e.g. a gene set, a metabolite panel, etc.).

docs.title: Induced
docs.text:
name: BMDDARM
description: 'Data Analysis Reporting Module (DARM) for Benchmark Dose Analysis and
  Quantification of Biological Potency


  This multi-omics compliant module specifies the information needed in order to assess
  benchmark dose (BMD) analysis of omics data and the subsequent derivation of an
  estimated BMD for a molecule (e.g. a transcript, protein or metabolite) or a set
  of molecules (e.g. a gene set, a metabolite panel, etc.).'
from_schema: https://w3id.org/eu-parc/maoorf
exact_mappings:
- oecd_oorf_2023:4.3
is_a: DARM
slot_usage:
  inputs:
    name: inputs
    exact_mappings:
    - oecd_oorf_2023:4.3.1
    range: BMDInputs
  outputs:
    name: outputs
    exact_mappings:
    - oecd_oorf_2023:4.3.7
    range: BMDOutputs
attributes:
  software_documentation:
    name: software_documentation
    description: 'Software Documentation


      The requirements in this section are intended to facilitate reproducibility
      of analyses and make quality assessment possible.'
    from_schema: https://w3id.org/eu-parc/maoorf/modules/darm/bmd
    exact_mappings:
    - oecd_oorf_2023:4.3.2
    owner: BMDDARM
    domain_of:
    - DAMDARM
    - BMDDARM
    - EBPDARM
    range: BMDSoftwareDocumentation
    recommended: true
  description_of_data_to_be_modelled:
    name: description_of_data_to_be_modelled
    description: 'Description of the Data to be Modelled


      In order to perform dose-response modelling a test article will need to be assessed
      for its effects on omics level changes at multiple dose levels. Henceforth in
      this document the actual data that are fit to dose response models will be called
      model substrate data (MSD).'
    from_schema: https://w3id.org/eu-parc/maoorf/modules/darm/bmd
    exact_mappings:
    - oecd_oorf_2023:4.3.3
    rank: 1000
    owner: BMDDARM
    domain_of:
    - BMDDARM
    range: BMDDataToBeModelled
    recommended: true
  pre_filtering_of_data:
    name: pre_filtering_of_data
    description: 'Pre-filtering of Data Prior to Dose-Response Modeling


      To reduce the burden of model fitting, which can be resource intensive, a prefiltering
      step is sometimes used to remove MSD that do not demonstrate a significant dose-related
      change.'
    from_schema: https://w3id.org/eu-parc/maoorf/modules/darm/bmd
    exact_mappings:
    - oecd_oorf_2023:4.3.4
    rank: 1000
    owner: BMDDARM
    domain_of:
    - BMDDARM
    range: BMDPreFilteringOfData
    recommended: true
  benchmark_dose_modeling:
    name: benchmark_dose_modeling
    description: 'Benchmark Dose Modeling


      BMD modelling is the process of fitting mathematical models to dose-response
      data to identify a modelled dose level where a predefined level (i.e. the benchmark
      response or BMR) of activity is predicted to occur.'
    from_schema: https://w3id.org/eu-parc/maoorf/modules/darm/bmd
    exact_mappings:
    - oecd_oorf_2023:4.3.5
    rank: 1000
    owner: BMDDARM
    domain_of:
    - BMDDARM
    range: BMDBenchmarkDoseModeling
    recommended: true
  determination_of_biological_entity_or_set_level_bmd_values:
    name: determination_of_biological_entity_or_set_level_bmd_values
    description: 'Determination of Biological Entity or Biological Set Level BMD values


      Often MSD are fractional representations of a biological entity (e.g. a gene
      or metabolite) or a biological set (e.g. a collection of genes or metabolites
      that make up a pathway). Organising the MSD into recognized biological entities
      helps in contextualising a biological response and allows for more robust BMD
      estimates at a molecular or biological process level.'
    from_schema: https://w3id.org/eu-parc/maoorf/modules/darm/bmd
    exact_mappings:
    - oecd_oorf_2023:4.3.6
    rank: 1000
    owner: BMDDARM
    domain_of:
    - BMDDARM
    range: BMDBiologicalSetLevelValues
    recommended: true
  inputs:
    name: inputs
    description: 'Inputs


      Input for data analysis, in the form of processed omics data (eg normalised
      gene expression data, normalised metabolome data) is generated using processes
      described in a DAPRM. The user should indicate what file(s) / data are used
      as the input for the analysis. Metadata files containing information associating
      omics samples with experimental parameters (eg treatments, dose levels, time
      points, sex, etc) may also be necessary for the analysis. The user should specify
      these files as well.'
    from_schema: https://w3id.org/eu-parc/maoorf
    exact_mappings:
    - oecd_oorf_2023:4.3.1
    rank: 1000
    owner: BMDDARM
    domain_of:
    - DARM
    range: BMDInputs
    recommended: true
  outputs:
    name: outputs
    description: 'Outputs and Supporting Files


      Complete the file manifest included as part of the reporting template. The manifest
      must include the listing of all files included in the regulatory application
      package specific to the analysis. Each file in the manifest must be accompanied
      by a description of the file. If the file being described is a tabular file,
      then the rows and columns must be described so that anyone can understand the
      contents of the file. Supporting files may include analysis scripts, software
      configurations or tables of metadata. The phrase `data object` refers to any
      machine readable input, output or metadata file.'
    from_schema: https://w3id.org/eu-parc/maoorf
    exact_mappings:
    - oecd_oorf_2023:4.3.7
    rank: 1000
    owner: BMDDARM
    domain_of:
    - DARM
    range: BMDOutputs
    recommended: true
  type:
    name: type
    description: Module type discriminator for the Data Analysis Reporting Module
    from_schema: https://w3id.org/eu-parc/maoorf/core/base
    designates_type: true
    owner: BMDDARM
    domain_of:
    - DAPRM
    - DARM
    range: string

docs.title: Class: BMDDataToBeModelled
docs.text:
Description of the Data to be Modelled

__

Dose levels, MSD annotation, and platform annotation version.

docs.title: Induced
docs.text:
name: BMDDataToBeModelled

  Dose levels, MSD annotation, and platform annotation version.'
from_schema: https://w3id.org/eu-parc/maoorf
exact_mappings:
- oecd_oorf_2023:4.3.3
attributes:
  dose_levels:
    name: dose_levels
    description: 'Dose Levels


      Identification of dose levels included in the BMD analysis and rationale for
      exclusion of any dose levels. Please specify the N for each dose.'
    from_schema: https://w3id.org/eu-parc/maoorf/modules/darm/bmd
    exact_mappings:
    - oecd_oorf_2023:4.3.3.1
    owner: BMDDataToBeModelled
    domain_of:
    - SSRMStudyDesign
    - TERMDoseSelection
    - BMDDataToBeModelled
    range: string
    recommended: true
  annotation_of_model_substrate_data:
    name: annotation_of_model_substrate_data
    description: 'Annotation of Model Substrate Data (MSD)


      With certain platforms (e.g. most transcriptomic platforms) there are existing
      annotations that will be associated with the data as a part of the data acquisition
      and processing procedures (as reported in the technology-specific DAPRMs). If
      MSD for BMD modelling corresponds to the measured features and annotations,
      without additional data abstraction (e.g. aggregation, summarization or merging
      of features), then this annotation and citation to the associated DAPRM is sufficient
      and must be provided. If features are merged or computed into meta-features
      (e.g. genes, gene sets, metabolite collections), then precise annotation of
      the meta-features must be reported here.'
    from_schema: https://w3id.org/eu-parc/maoorf/modules/darm/bmd
    exact_mappings:
    - oecd_oorf_2023:4.3.3.2
    rank: 1000

    domain_of:
    - BMDDataToBeModelled
    range: string
    recommended: true
  version_of_platform_annotation:
    name: version_of_platform_annotation
    description: 'Version of Platform Annotation that Corresponds to Technology


      Annotations for the measured MSD in a data set are in certain cases updated
      frequently. The annotations are often associated with a date and/or a version.
      This information must be captured to ensure reproducibility of the findings.'
    from_schema: https://w3id.org/eu-parc/maoorf/modules/darm/bmd
    exact_mappings:
    - oecd_oorf_2023:4.3.3.3
    rank: 1000

    domain_of:
    - BMDDataToBeModelled
    range: string
    recommended: true

docs.text:
Pre-filtering of Data Prior to Dose-Response Modeling

__

Statistical and non-statistical pre-filtering parameters prior to BMD modelling.

docs.title: Induced
docs.text:
name: BMDPreFilteringOfData
description: 'Pre-filtering of Data Prior to Dose-Response Modeling


  Statistical and non-statistical pre-filtering parameters prior to BMD modelling.'
from_schema: https://w3id.org/eu-parc/maoorf
exact_mappings:
- oecd_oorf_2023:4.3.4
attributes:
  statistical_test_performed:
    name: statistical_test_performed
    description: 'Statistical Test Performed to Identify Dose-Responsive MSD


      There are a variety of methods for performing statistical filtering of dose
      response data. These range from pairwise methods such as ANOVA, to trend-based
      tests such as the Williams trend test. Record the statistical method that was
      applied to the data. If additional filtering was not applied indicate NA (not
      applicable)'
    from_schema: https://w3id.org/eu-parc/maoorf/modules/darm/bmd
    exact_mappings:
    - oecd_oorf_2023:4.3.4.1
    owner: BMDPreFilteringOfData
    domain_of:
    - BMDPreFilteringOfData
    - EBPEnrichedPathways
    range: string
    recommended: true
  statistical_threshold_applied:
    name: statistical_threshold_applied
    description: 'Statistical Threshold Applied


      Indicate the statistical threshold that was applied when performing any statistical
      test to pre-filter the data.'
    from_schema: https://w3id.org/eu-parc/maoorf/modules/darm/bmd
    exact_mappings:
    - oecd_oorf_2023:4.3.4.2
    owner: BMDPreFilteringOfData
    domain_of:
    - BMDPreFilteringOfData
    - EBPEnrichedPathways
    range: string
    recommended: true
  statistical_multiple_testing_correction_method:
    name: statistical_multiple_testing_correction_method
    description: 'Statistical Multiple Testing Correction Method


      Because of the large number of replicate statistical tests that are performed
      when analysing an omics data set, an adjusted statistical threshold is often
      applied that corrects for a large number of tests, therefore reducing the false
      discovery rate. Report the method that was used to perform the multiple testing
      correction. If no correction was applied, indicate NA (not applicable).'
    from_schema: https://w3id.org/eu-parc/maoorf/modules/darm/bmd
    exact_mappings:
    - oecd_oorf_2023:4.3.4.3
    rank: 1000
    owner: BMDPreFilteringOfData
    domain_of:
    - BMDPreFilteringOfData
    range: string
    recommended: true
  additional_statistical_test_parameters:
    name: additional_statistical_test_parameters
    description: 'Additional Statistical Test Parameters


      This section is to describe any additional parameters that were applied and
      can impact statistical testing results. An example would be the number of iterations
      that were performed when employing a bootstrap method for p-value determination.'
    comments:
    - Describe any additional statistical parameters that were applied for data filtering
      that may impact results. An example is the number of iterations that were performed
      when employing a bootstrap method for p-value calculation.
    from_schema: https://w3id.org/eu-parc/maoorf/modules/darm/bmd
    exact_mappings:
    - oecd_oorf_2023:4.3.4.4
    rank: 1000
    owner: BMDPreFilteringOfData
    domain_of:
    - BMDPreFilteringOfData
    range: string
    recommended: true
  additional_filtering:
    name: additional_filtering
    description: 'Additional Filtering


      In addition to a statistical filter, additional filters are sometimes applied
      to ensure that only responses representing biologically meaningful changes are
      retained. One of the most common is a fold change filter. If more complicated
      filter methods are applied a detailed description of the method and all critical
      parameters should be provided. If no additional filtering was applied, indicate
      NA (not applicable).'
    comments:
    - Describe any non-statistical parameters that were applied for data filtering
      that may impact results. An example is a fold-change criteria.
    from_schema: https://w3id.org/eu-parc/maoorf/modules/darm/bmd
    exact_mappings:
    - oecd_oorf_2023:4.3.4.5
    owner: BMDPreFilteringOfData

docs.title: Class: DAMDARM
docs.text:
Data Analysis Reporting Module (DARM) for Discovery of Differentially Abundant Molecules - Univariate Methods

__

This multi-omics compliant module specifies the information needed by a regulatory scientist in order to assess univariate statistical analysis as used to discover differentially abundant molecules (DAMs); i.e. for transcriptomics, to identify differentially expressed genes (DEG). Henceforth DEG are referred to as DAM.

  Abundant Molecules - Univariate Methods


  This multi-omics compliant module specifies the information needed by a regulatory
  scientist in order to assess univariate statistical analysis as used to discover
  differentially abundant molecules (DAMs); i.e. for transcriptomics, to identify
  differentially expressed genes (DEG). Henceforth DEG are referred to as DAM.'

docs.title: Class: DAPRM
docs.text:
Data Acquisition and Processing Reporting Modules (DAPRMs)

__

Data Acquisition and Processing Reporting Modules (DAPRMs) capture and report descriptions of the omics assays, data acquisition and associated data processing prior to statistical analysis. These modules are unique to each omics data type. Furthermore, the reporting described is generalisable and adaptable, because (1) it is not the intention of this Guidance Document to prescribe the types of assays that the regulatory toxicology community should use; (2) technologies will continue to evolve and we want the OORF to remain relevant; and (3) omics assays often do not fit well into predefined boxes.

docs.title: Class: DARM
docs.text:
Data Analysis Reporting Modules (DARMs)

__

These modules serve to capture and report descriptions of the statistical analysis that is undertaken in the omics study, for example for the purposes of discovering differentially abundant molecules (eg differentially expressed genes in a transcriptomic study). The modules were designed to accommodate various types of omics data and can thus be applied to multi-omic data sets. There is one or more DARM per study (a minimum of one is mandatory) dependent upon the type(s) of data analysis applied to the datasets.

docs.title: Class: MVADARM
docs.text:
Data Analysis Reporting Module (DARM) for Multivariate Statistical Analysis Module

__

This multi-omics compliant module specifies the information needed by a regulatory scientist in order to assess multivariate statistical analysis. The goals of this module are to specify what needs to be reported while not being prescriptive about the analysis performed. We leave judgement about the appropriateness of the analysis plan to the users.

docs.title: Induced
docs.text:

description: 'Data Analysis Reporting Module (DARM) for Multivariate Statistical Analysis
  Module


  This multi-omics compliant module specifies the information needed by a regulatory

    rank: 1000
    owner: MVADARM
    domain_of:
    - MVADARM
    range: MVAVariableImportance
    recommended: true
  inputs:
    name: inputs
    description: 'Inputs


      Input for data analysis, in the form of processed omics data (eg normalised
      gene expression data, normalised metabolome data) is generated using processes
      described in a DAPRM. The user should indicate what file(s) / data are used

      points, sex, etc) may also be necessary for the analysis. The user should specify

    rank: 1000
    owner: MVADARM
    domain_of:
    - DARM
    range: MVAInputs
    recommended: true

      Complete the file manifest included as part of the reporting template. The manifest

    exact_mappings:
    - oecd_oorf_2023:4.2.9
    rank: 1000

    domain_of:

    range: MVAOutputs
    recommended: true

docs.title: Class: MassSpectrometryDAPRM
docs.text:
Data Acquisition and Processing Reporting Module (DAPRM) for Mass Spectrometry Metabolomics

__

In this Data Acquisition and Processing Reporting Module we describe the reporting required for a mass spectrometry-based metabolomics study, including sample processing, metabolite extraction and preparation of standards; analytical QA/QC samples; acquisition and processing of mass spectrometry data; demonstrating the quality of the data; and the data matrices produced by this technology, including metabolite annotation/identification and intensities.

  metabolite extraction and preparation of standards; analytical QA/QC samples; acquisition

docs.title: Class: MicroarrayDAPRM
docs.text:
Data Acquisition and Processing Reporting Module (DAPRM) for Microarray

__

This module provides a reporting framework for describing a microarray technology, documenting transcriptomic study experimental design including platform-specific sample processing (such as addition of controls, labelling and hybridisation), details of raw data acquisition and format and how normalisation, data filtering and outlier identification and removal was conducted.

docs.text:

description: 'Data Acquisition and Processing Reporting Module (DAPRM) for Microarray


  This module provides a reporting framework for describing a microarray technology,
  documenting transcriptomic study experimental design including platform-specific
  sample processing (such as addition of controls, labelling and hybridisation), details
  of raw data acquisition and format and how normalisation, data filtering and outlier
  identification and removal was conducted.'

      Images from a scanned microarray slide contain features (spots) of various signal

      downstream analysis such as identification of differentially expressed genes.'

      information a regulatory scientist needs to understand the types of filtering
      that were applied to gene expression data.'

OECD Omics Reporting Framework (OORF)

To report an omics study, scientists select the relevant reporting modules (and hence reporting elements), minimally consisting of an SSRM, TERM, one DAPRM and one DARM. A file manifest tab is included in the tabular reporting spreadsheets, the purpose of which is to list all data objects relevant to a study.

docs.title: Class: QRTPCRDAPRM
docs.text:
Data Acquisition and Processing Reporting Module (DAPRM) for Quantitative Reverse Transcription Polymerase Chain Reaction (qRT-PCR)

__

This module provides a reporting framework for describing a qPCR-based toxicogenomic experiment, including sample preparation, assay design, and data collection and processing. This module is largely based on the existing minimum information for publication of quantitative real-time PCR experiments (MIQE) guidelines but has been adapted for the OORF.

docs.title: Class: RNASeqDAPRM
docs.text:
Data Acquisition and Processing Reporting Module (DAPRM) for RNA Seq and Targeted RNA-Seq Data

__

This module provides a reporting framework for describing the RNA-Seq or targeted RNA-Seq technology and methodology used in a toxicology experiment. It aims to guide the users on how to document all of the study design parameters required to understand and analyse the experiment, including the platform-specific sample processing steps, library preparation protocol details, raw data acquisition and how quality control, alignment, gene quantification, normalisation, data filtering and outlier identification were conducted.

docs.title: Class: SSRM
docs.text:
Study Summary Reporting Module (SSRM)

__

This module describes a subset of mandatory reporting elements in order to provide a high-level summary of the application of omics to a regulatory toxicology study. With the exception of the reporting element in Section 1 - Study identifiers, see below, each section is derived from reporting elements described elsewhere within this Guidance Document. Specifically, this includes summarising the TERM, any Data Acquisition & Processing Reporting Module(s) (DAPRMs) used and any Data Analysis Reporting Module(s) (DARMs) used.

docs.title: Class: SoftwareDocumentation
docs.text:
Software Documentation

__

The requirements in this section are intended to facilitate reproducibility of analyses and make quality assessment possible. Freely available open source, commercially available, or proprietary software may be used. The name and version of all software that is used must be specified. In addition, all add-ons, plug-ins, packages, or libraries (hereafter "libraries") that are called, used, required, loaded, or otherwise brought into the software must be specified. This specification must include the name and version of such libraries, and a hyperlink to download the libraries. In those cases where the libraries are locally developed and controlled, such that a hyperlink to download does not exist, specify the following: "this library is not available for download" and should then make the code available as specified in the reporting template.

docs.title: Class: TERM
docs.text:
Toxicology Experiment Reporting Module (TERM)

__

The TERM serves to capture and report the key descriptors of the in vivo or in vitro toxicology study from which samples are derived for omics analyses. One TERM should be reported per study, irrespective of whether one or more omics approaches are applied or whether one or more types of data analysis are performed.

docs.title: Induced
docs.text:
name: TERM
description: 'Toxicology Experiment Reporting Module (TERM)


  The TERM serves to capture and report the key descriptors of the in vivo or in vitro
  toxicology study from which samples are derived for omics analyses. One TERM should
  be reported per study, irrespective of whether one or more omics approaches are
  applied or whether one or more types of data analysis are performed.'
from_schema: https://w3id.org/eu-parc/maoorf
exact_mappings:
- oecd_oorf_2023:2
attributes:
  study_rationale:
    name: study_rationale
    description: 'Study Rationale


      A clear and concise report of the study rationale is necessary to understand
      the suitability of the experimental design for the regulatory question being
      addressed, including the selection of experimental model, sex, target tissue,
      dosing regimen, etc. These fundamental aspects of the experimental design are
      clearly dependent on the study rationale.'
    from_schema: https://w3id.org/eu-parc/maoorf/modules/term
    exact_mappings:
    - oecd_oorf_2023:2.1
    owner: TERM
    domain_of:
    - SSRM
    - TERM
    range: TERMStudyRationale
    recommended: true
  test_and_control_items:
    name: test_and_control_items
    description: 'Test and Control items


      Regulatory scientists must have all test items, vehicle, and control identification
      and characterisation information to accurately interpret omic study results.
      The following information should be reported for all test items: A) test substance,
      B) vehicle, and C) controls, including: test item name, mixture formulation
      composition, preparation of test item, physicochemical properties, chemical
      stability, commercial source and substance-specific identifiers.'
    from_schema: https://w3id.org/eu-parc/maoorf/modules/term
    exact_mappings:
    - oecd_oorf_2023:2.2
    rank: 1000
    owner: TERM
    domain_of:
    - TERM
    range: TERMTestAndControlItems
    recommended: true
  test_system_characteristics:
    name: test_system_characteristics
    description: 'Test System Characteristics


      Similar to traditional toxicity testing, it is critical that regulatory scientists
      applying omics data for risk assessment be provided with comprehensive information
      regarding the characteristics of the test system from which the data are derived.
      Test system refers to the biological system that is exposed to the test items
      to obtain experimental data.'
    from_schema: https://w3id.org/eu-parc/maoorf/modules/term
    exact_mappings:
    - oecd_oorf_2023:2.3
    rank: 1000
    owner: TERM
    domain_of:
    - TERM
    range: TERMTestSystemCharacteristics
    recommended: true
  study_design:
    name: study_design
    description: 'Study Design


      Study designs are based on the assessment of all available information for factors
      that have the potential to influence study results. A detailed description of
      all elements and parameters included in the study design will increase transparency
      and confidence in the data, and as a result, will have greater utility in regulatory
      assessment.'
    from_schema: https://w3id.org/eu-parc/maoorf/modules/term
    exact_mappings:
    - oecd_oorf_2023:2.4
    owner: TERM
    domain_of:
    - SSRMStudyRationale
    - TERM
    range: TERMStudyDesign
    recommended: true
  treatment_conditions:
    name: treatment_conditions
    description: 'Treatment Conditions


      The objective of the omic study informs the selection of the treatment conditions,
      which, in turn, impact the final outcome. Omic analyses may produce different
      results depending on the route of administration, the dose levels and the time
      and schedule of the exposure. Thus, a thorough description of treatment conditions
      is necessary for interpreting omic study results.'
    from_schema: https://w3id.org/eu-parc/maoorf/modules/term
    exact_mappings:
    - oecd_oorf_2023:2.5
    owner: TERM
    domain_of:
    - SSRMStudyRationale
    - TERM
    range: TERMTreatmentConditions
    recommended: true
  study_exit_and_sample_collection:
    name: study_exit_and_sample_collection
    description: 'Study Exit and Sample Collection


      Omics can be conducted using samples from animal or in vitro studies to produce
      a "snapshot" of transcript, protein or metabolite levels and enable analysis
      of perturbations in biological pathways and processes. Proper sample preparation
      is a key step in omics studies and adequate care must be taken to ensure sample
      fidelity.'
    from_schema: https://w3id.org/eu-parc/maoorf/modules/term
    exact_mappings:
    - oecd_oorf_2023:2.6
    rank: 1000
    owner: TERM
    domain_of:
    - TERM
    range: TERMStudyExitAndSampleCollection
    recommended: true
  sample_identification_codes:
    name: sample_identification_codes
    description: 'Sample Identification Codes


      Sample management is a critical component of regulatory and non-regulatory experimentation
      which should be carefully planned. A standard operating procedure (SOP) should
      be established to ensure identification, tracking, unbiased testing and data
      collection records for each sample.'
    from_schema: https://w3id.org/eu-parc/maoorf/modules/term
    exact_mappings:
    - oecd_oorf_2023:2.7
    rank: 1000
    owner: TERM
    domain_of:
    - TERM
    range: TERMSampleIdentificationCodes
    recommended: true
  supporting_data_streams:
    name: supporting_data_streams
    description: 'Supporting Data Streams


      To benefit optimally from the data generated, additional information should
      be reported to the extent possible. This information can range from OECD Test
      Guidelines for a particular animal study to methodological Standard Operating
      Procedures (SOP) to scientific publications in which analysis of (a subset of)
      the data has been described. Toxicity or cytotoxicity experiments necessary
      to establish the appropriate doses/concentrations can also be reported here.'
    from_schema: https://w3id.org/eu-parc/maoorf/modules/term
    exact_mappings:
    - oecd_oorf_2023:2.8
    rank: 1000
    owner: TERM
    domain_of:
    - TERM
    range: TERMSupportingDataStreams

docs.title: Class: TERMStudyRationale
docs.text:
Study Rationale

__

Overall, a clear rationale describing why an omics study was undertaken is required to assess the suitability of the experimental design and its intended use for regulatory decision making. This section is intended to be a narrative description of the reasoning for the study and its design. Details of the study parameters are to be provided in later sections.

docs.title: Induced
docs.text:
name: TERMStudyRationale
description: 'Study Rationale


  Overall, a clear rationale describing why an omics study was undertaken is required
  to assess the suitability of the experimental design and its intended use for regulatory
  decision making. This section is intended to be a narrative description of the reasoning
  for the study and its design. Details of the study parameters are to be provided
  in later sections.'
from_schema: https://w3id.org/eu-parc/maoorf
exact_mappings:
- oecd_oorf_2023:2.1
attributes:
  background_information:
    name: background_information
    description: 'Background information


      Provide necessary background information for the end-user to understand the
      rationale for why the study was undertaken, including the regulatory question(s).'
    from_schema: https://w3id.org/eu-parc/maoorf/modules/term
    exact_mappings:

    owner: TERMStudyRationale

    recommended: true
  objectives:
    name: objectives
    description: 'Objectives


      Clearly define the objectives of the study toward informing the regulatory question.
      Describe whether the study results are intended to be interpreted in isolation
      or in combination with results from other studies.'
    from_schema: https://w3id.org/eu-parc/maoorf/modules/term

    - TERMStudyRationale
    range: string
    recommended: true
  test_guideline_compliance:

      If appropriate, please refer to which OECD Test Guidelines have been followed
      in the performance of the method.'
    comments:
    - If appropriate, please refer to which OECD Test Guidelines have been followed
      in the performance of the method.
    from_schema: https://w3id.org/eu-parc/maoorf/modules/term
    exact_mappings:
    - oecd_oorf_2023:2.1.3
    rank: 1000
    owner: TERMStudyRationale
    domain_of:
    - TERMStudyRationale
    range: string
  mechanistic_understanding:
    name: mechanistic_understanding
    description: 'Mechanistic understanding


      Briefly describe any prior toxicological, mode of action, or mechanistic information
      that is useful to understanding the study rationale (e.g. established mechanism
      of action and its relationship to the toxicological effect of interest).'
    from_schema: https://w3id.org/eu-parc/maoorf/modules/term
    exact_mappings:
    - oecd_oorf_2023:2.1.4
    rank: 1000
    owner: TERMStudyRationale
    domain_of:
    - TERMStudyRationale
    range: string
    recommended: true
  model_selection:
    name: model_selection
    description: 'Model selection


      Rationale for the selection of animal species, strain, model, tissue, or in
      vitro test system.'
    from_schema: https://w3id.org/eu-parc/maoorf/modules/term
    exact_mappings:
    - oecd_oorf_2023:2.1.5
    owner: TERMStudyRationale
    domain_of:
    - TERMStudyRationale
    - BMDBenchmarkDoseModeling
    range: TERMModelSelection
    recommended: true
  dose_concentration_level_and_interval_selection:
    name: dose_concentration_level_and_interval_selection
    description: 'Dose / concentration level and interval selection


      Provide a brief rationale for the selection of the employed dose (in vivo) or
      test concentration (in vitro) levels and intervals. For example, selection for
      in vivo experimentation may be based on known toxicological effects or molecular
      changes documented for the test item identified in prior studies, allowing for
      "read-across" between omics data generated and other in-life findings, or clinical
      pathological changes and pathological observations. Note that dose interval
      information should include the time of exposure during the day. Similarly, in
      the case of in vitro experiments, if a relationship is sought to in vivo exposures,
      test item concentrations may be chosen using a quantitative in vitro/in vivo
      extrapolation (IVIVE) rationale; a rationale for the top concentration selected
      should be included.'
    comments:
    - Report dose levels & rationale for dose level selection
    from_schema: https://w3id.org/eu-parc/maoorf/modules/term
    exact_mappings:
    - oecd_oorf_2023:2.1.6
    rank: 1000
    owner: TERMStudyRationale
    domain_of:
    - TERMStudyRationale
    range: string
    recommended: true
  route_of_administration:
    name: route_of_administration
    description: 'Route of administration


      Where relevant, provide a rationale for the choice of route of administration,
      referring to objectives of the study, potential route of human exposure, the
      physical and chemical characteristics of the test item and the relevance for
      the evaluated endpoint.'
    comments:
    - Report route of administration and rationale for selecting this route.
    from_schema: https://w3id.org/eu-parc/maoorf/modules/term
    exact_mappings:
    - oecd_oorf_2023:2.1.7
    owner: TERMStudyRationale
    domain_of:
    - SSRMTreatmentConditions
    - TERMStudyRationale
    range: string
    recommended: true
  time_point_selection:
    name: time_point_selection
    description: 'Time point selection


      Provide a brief rationale for the exposure durations and sampling time points.
      Transcriptome, proteome, and metabolome profiles are dependent on both the duration
      of exposure and the time of sample collection. Responses reflect cellular adaptation
      over time, with early time points reflecting molecular initiating and early
      key events, and later time points reflecting pathological changes or adaptation.
      For in vivo studies, the interval between the final dosing and sample procurement
      should be specified. The same is true for sampling-time post-treatment for in
      vitro studies.'
    comments:
    - Report time points & rational for time point selection
    from_schema: https://w3id.org/eu-parc/maoorf/modules/term
    exact_mappings:
    - oecd_oorf_2023:2.1.8
    rank: 1000
    owner: TERMStudyRationale
    domain_of:
    - TERMStudyRationale
    range: string
    recommended: true
  samples_and_replicates:
    name: samples_and_replicates
    description: 'Samples and Replicates


      Provide a clear rationale for the choice of biological, technical, and analytical
      replicate numbers.'
    from_schema: https://w3id.org/eu-parc/maoorf/modules/term
    exact_mappings:
    - oecd_oorf_2023:2.1.9
    rank: 1000
    owner: TERMStudyRationale
    domain_of:
    - TERMStudyRationale
    range: TERMSamplesAndReplicatesRationale
    recommended: true
  limitations:
    name: limitations
    description: 'Limitations


      To facilitate regulatory evaluation, when appropriate, indicate the study limitations
      that could affect the outcome or interpretation of the results. These can include
      technical or mechanistic limitations in relation to known modes of action. For
      example, if the experiment includes poorly described test systems that would
      be a source of uncontrollable variability (e.g. a limitation of cell systems
      may be a lack of information about metabolic capacity), such information should
      be available to the evaluator. Likewise, some of the test items used might have
      physicochemical properties (lipophilicity, volatility, etc.) that might lead
      to a cell exposure that is different from the expected exposure (through interaction
      with plastic or proteins in culture plates and medium) or that produce large
      and confounding signals in omics outputs (e.g. NMR or MS spectra). In the case
      of in vivo studies, discussion of limitations should include any potential source
      of bias of the animal model or imprecision associated with the result.'
    comments:
    - If known, describe study limitations that could affect the outcome of interpretation
      of results.
    from_schema: https://w3id.org/eu-parc/maoorf/modules/term
    exact_mappings:
    - oecd_oorf_2023:2.1.10
    rank: 1000
    owner: TERMStudyRationale
    domain_of:
    - TERMStudyRationale
    range: string

- oecd_oorf_2023:2.5
attributes:
  route_of_administration_in_vivo:
    name: route_of_administration_in_vivo
    description: 'Route of administration (in vivo)


      For in vivo studies, indicate the selected route of administration for the test
      item. Examples are oral (e.g. gavage or diet), dermal, inhalation, parenteral,
      implantation, etc. If applicable, for implantation experiments, state the exposure
      regime (e.g. static, semi-static, flow through). Also state other information
      that may be required to understand the route of exposure for the test item.'
    comments:
    - Indicate the route of administration used in the in vivo toxicology study (e.g.
      roal, dermal, inhalation, etc). If not an in vivo study, enter "NOT IN VIVO
      STUDY"
    from_schema: https://w3id.org/eu-parc/maoorf/modules/term
    exact_mappings:
    - oecd_oorf_2023:2.5.1
    rank: 1000
    owner: TERMTreatmentConditions
    domain_of:
    - TERMTreatmentConditions
    range: string
    recommended: true
  route_of_administration_in_vitro:
    name: route_of_administration_in_vitro
    description: 'Route of administration (in vitro)


      For in vitro studies, describe how the test item was administered to the in
      vitro system. Examples are direct addition of the test item to cultures, substitution
      of culture medium, exposure at air-liquid interface, etc. Also state other information
      that may be required to understand how the test time item was administered to
      the in vitro system.'
    comments:
    - Indicate the route of administration used in the in vitro toxocology study (e.g.
      dissolution in media, air-liquid interface, etc.). If not an in vitro study,
      enter "NOT IN VITRO STUDY"
    from_schema: https://w3id.org/eu-parc/maoorf/modules/term
    exact_mappings:
    - oecd_oorf_2023:2.5.2
    rank: 1000
    owner: TERMTreatmentConditions
    domain_of:
    - TERMTreatmentConditions
    range: string
    recommended: true
  housing_condition_modifications_in_vivo:
    name: housing_condition_modifications_in_vivo
    description: 'Housing condition modifications relevant to test article treatment
      (in vivo)


      Describe any modifications of the standard culture/housing conditions occurring
      before and during the test item exposure (refer to ''Housing, husbandry, and
      culture conditions'' in Section 2.3 - Test System Characteristics). Examples
      include fasting period, use of anaesthesia and/or analgesia or other modifications
      to standard housing conditions that may have occurred before or during exposure
      to test items.'
    comments:
    - Describe any modifications of the in vivo housing conditions that occur before
      or during test item exposure that may influence the outcome. Examples include
      fasting periods prior to dosing, application of anesthesia or analgesics, etcs.
      If not an in vivo study enter "NO IN VIVO STUDY"
    from_schema: https://w3id.org/eu-parc/maoorf/modules/term
    exact_mappings:
    - oecd_oorf_2023:2.5.3
    rank: 1000
    owner: TERMTreatmentConditions
    domain_of:
    - TERMTreatmentConditions
    range: string
  culture_condition_modifications_in_vitro:
    name: culture_condition_modifications_in_vitro
    description: 'Culture condition modifications relevant to test article treatment
      (in vitro)


      Describe any modification of the culture conditions occurring before and during
      the test item exposure (refer to ''Cell Culture Conditions'' in Section 2.3
      - Test System Characteristics). Examples include switching to serum-free or
      serum-depleted medium, use of items for limiting media evaporation or other
      modifications to standard culture conditions that may have occurred before or
      during exposure to test items.'
    comments:
    - Describe any modifications of the in vitro cell culture conditions that occur
      before or during test item exposure that may influence the outcome. Examples
      include switching from growth media to test media for chemical exposures or
      using cultureware that limits evaporation or changes gas diffusion properties.
      If not an in vitro study, enter "NOT IN VITRO STUDY".
    from_schema: https://w3id.org/eu-parc/maoorf/modules/term
    exact_mappings:

    comments:
    - Describe all the steps involves in test item preparation prior to administration

      input "NA". If unkonwn, input "UNKNOWN"
    from_schema: https://w3id.org/eu-parc/maoorf/modules/term

If MSD for BMD modelling corresponds to the measured features and annotations, without additional data abstraction (e.g. aggregation, summarization or merging of features), then this annotation and citation to the associated DAPRM is sufficient and must be provided. Provide a brief rationale for the selection of the employed dose (in vivo) or test concentration (in vitro) levels and intervals. For example, selection for in vivo experimentation may be based on known toxicological effects or molecular changes documented for the test item identified in prior studies, allowing for "read-across" between omics data generated and other in-life findings, or clinical pathological changes and pathological observations. Note that dose interval information should include the time of exposure during the day. Similarly, in the case of in vitro experiments, if a relationship is sought to in vivo exposures, test item concentrations may be chosen using a quantitative in vitro/in vivo extrapolation (IVIVE) rationale; a rationale for the top concentration selected should be included.

docs.title: Slot: limitations
docs.text:
Limitations

__

To facilitate regulatory evaluation, when appropriate, indicate the study limitations that could affect the outcome or interpretation of the results. These can include technical or mechanistic limitations in relation to known modes of action. For example, if the experiment includes poorly described test systems that would be a source of uncontrollable variability (e.g. a limitation of cell systems may be a lack of information about metabolic capacity), such information should be available to the evaluator. Likewise, some of the test items used might have physicochemical properties (lipophilicity, volatility, etc.) that might lead to a cell exposure that is different from the expected exposure (through interaction with plastic or proteins in culture plates and medium) or that produce large and confounding signals in omics outputs (e.g. NMR or MS spectra). In the case of in vivo studies, discussion of limitations should include any potential source of bias of the animal model or imprecision associated with the result.

docs.title: Slot: method_for_final_estimation_of_msd_bmd
docs.text:
Method for Final Estimation of MSD BMD

__

There are two general approaches for identifying a final potency estimate for a given feature - best model selection and model averaging. With the best model approach a single best model is used to derive the BMD; whereas, model averaging uses a weighted average to derive a final BMD estimate. In the case of non-parametric modelling, typically only a single model fitting process is performed, hence there isn't a best model or models to average. In this case the method for final estimation of BMD is simply the modelling approach.

docs.title: Slot: method_of_estimating_set_bmd_bmdl_bmdu
docs.text:
Method of Estimating the BMD, BMDL, and BMDU of the Individual Biological Entity or Biological Sets

__

When MSD are sorted into sets this means a set contains several BMD values representative of each MSD in the set. When this happens, and the biological set is determined to be active (in the case of sets), a representative BMD, BMDL and BMDU value for the entire set can be determined. The choice of method will impact the estimate of potency for most biological entity sets so it is important that the method for deriving a representative BMD, BMDL and BMDU value be very clearly documented.

docs.title: Slot: time_point_selection
docs.text:
Time point selection

__

Provide a brief rationale for the exposure durations and sampling time points. Transcriptome, proteome, and metabolome profiles are dependent on both the duration of exposure and the time of sample collection. Responses reflect cellular adaptation over time, with early time points reflecting molecular initiating and early key events, and later time points reflecting pathological changes or adaptation. For in vivo studies, the interval between the final dosing and sample procurement should be specified. The same is true for sampling-time post-treatment for in vitro studies.

docs.title: Slot: variance_assumption
docs.text:
Variance Assumption

__

Toxicology data are often heteroscedastic (i.e. the spread on the response distribution increases with dose). This is often referred to as non-constant variance. Different assumptions are made when data are assumed to be hetero vs homoscedastic, which can impact model fitting and BMD derivation. It is therefore necessary to document if constant or non-constant variance was assumed.
